## Owner Creation Code Map (spring-petclinic-rest)

All paths are under the repo root `/home/daniel/spring-petclinic-rest-long-degradation-test/work/202608011310/spring-just-solve-chain9`.

### 1. Owner JPA entity + city field
`src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Owner.java`
- `@Entity @Table(name = "owners")`, extends `Person` (which holds `firstName`/`lastName`).
- City field (lines 43-45):
```java
@Column(name = "city")
@NotEmpty
private String city;
```
- Other columns: `address` (`@NotEmpty`), `telephone` (`@NotEmpty`, `@Digits`, `@Pattern ^[0-9]{10}$`), `email`, `registrationDate` (LocalDate), `membershipNumber` (Integer), `customerCode` (String), and `pets` (`@OneToMany`). Getters/setters `getCity()`/`setCity()` at lines 76-82.

### 2. REST controller POST for owner creation
`src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`
- Class implements the generated `OwnersApi`; base path `/api`.
- `addOwner(OwnerFieldsDto ownerFieldsDto)` (lines 105-127) is the POST handler. Flow:
  - `Owner owner = ownerMapper.toOwner(ownerFieldsDto);` maps DTO to entity.
  - Normalizes telephone, defaults `registrationDate` to `LocalDate.now()` if absent.
  - Duplicate-telephone and duplicate-email checks throw `DuplicateOwnerException`.
  - Sets `membershipNumber` = current owner count + 1.
  - **City-specific logic**: `owner.setCustomerCode(nextCustomerCode(owner.getCity()));`
  - Persists via `this.clinicService.saveOwner(owner)`, returns 201 with `Location` header.
- `nextCustomerCode(String city)` (lines 184-190) builds a code `"<UPPERCASE_CITY>-<NNNN>"` where NNNN = (count of existing owners in same city, case-insensitive) + 1, zero-padded to 4 digits:
```java
long ownersInCity = this.clinicService.findAllOwners().stream()
    .filter(existing -> existing.getCity() != null
        && existing.getCity().equalsIgnoreCase(city))
    .count();
return String.format("%s-%04d", city.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT), ownersInCity + 1);
```
- Note: `updateOwner` (lines 211-223) also does `currentOwner.setCity(ownerFieldsDto.getCity())`.
- There is also a V2 controller: `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/controller/v2/OwnerRestControllerV2.java` (pagination-oriented; check if relevant).

### 3. Service layer (ClinicService)
- Interface: `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/service/ClinicService.java` — owner methods (lines 56-61): `findOwnerById`, `findAllOwners`, `findOwners(String, Pageable)`, `saveOwner`, `deleteOwner`, `findOwnerByLastName`.
- Impl: `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/service/ClinicServiceImpl.java` — `saveOwner` (lines 232-237) simply delegates:
```java
@Override @Transactional
public void saveOwner(Owner owner) throws DataAccessException {
    ownerRepository.save(owner);
}
```
No city handling in the service layer; it is purely a passthrough to the repository.

### 4. Owner repository
- Interface: `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/repository/OwnerRepository.java` — methods: `findByLastName(String)`, `findByLastName(String, Pageable)`, `findById(int)`, `save(Owner)`, `findAll()`, `findAll(Pageable)`, `delete(Owner)`. No city-based query method exists.
- Implementations:
  - `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/repository/jpa/JpaOwnerRepositoryImpl.java`
  - `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/repository/jdbc/JdbcOwnerRepositoryImpl.java`
  - `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/repository/springdatajpa/SpringDataOwnerRepository.java`

### 5. Tests related to owner creation

Test fixtures use `"city":"Madison"` / `"Springfield"`; helper sets `owner.setCity("Madison")` at line 54.
- Service-layer tests exercising owner persistence (all reference city):
  - `src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/service/clinicService/AbstractClinicServiceTests.java` (base)
  - `ClinicServiceJpaTests.java`, `ClinicServiceHsqlJdbcTests.java`, `ClinicServiceH2JdbcTests.java`, `ClinicServiceSpringDataJpaTests.java` (same directory)
- Acceptance tests referencing city: `src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/Cp02Tests.java`, `Cp03Tests.java`, `Cp10Tests.java`, `Cp12Tests.java`, and base `AcceptanceBase.java`.

### 6. MapStruct mapper OwnerDto/OwnerFieldsDto -> Owner
- Interface: `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/mapper/OwnerMapper.java`
  - `@Mapper(uses = PetMapper.class)`.
  - `Owner toOwner(OwnerDto ownerDto)` (line 59).
  - `Owner toOwner(OwnerFieldsDto ownerDto)` (lines 61-63) with `@Mapping(target="id", ignore=true)` and `@Mapping(target="pets", ignore=true)` — this is the one used by `addOwner`. City is auto-mapped by name (no explicit mapping needed).
- Generated impl: `target/generated-sources/annotations/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/mapper/OwnerMapperImpl.java` confirms city mapping in all three: `toOwner(OwnerFieldsDto)` at line 84 does `owner.setCity(ownerDto.getCity())`; `toOwner(OwnerDto)` at line 62; `toOwnerDto` at line 35.

The related `OwnerDto.java` and `OwnerPageDto.java` are in the same generated `dto` directory, and the OpenAPI contract interface is `.../rest/api/OwnersApi.java`.

Note: `customerCode` (the city-derived field) is set only in the controller's `addOwner`; it has no bean-validation annotations and is not part of `OwnerFieldsDto`, so it is populated server-side rather than from the request.

## Summary

I implemented the city title-casing and reuse behaviour for owner creation in `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`.

**Change** (`src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`):
- Added `owner.setCity(resolveCity(owner.getCity()))` before persisting, so the stored/returned `city` follows the new rule.
- `resolveCity(String city)` — scans existing owners for one whose city matches case-insensitively; if found, reuses that owner's **exact spelling**; otherwise falls back to title-casing.
- `titleCase(String city)` — upper-cases the first letter of each whitespace-separated word and lower-cases the rest, preserving original spacing (e.g. `"gOtHaM cITY"` → `"Gotham City"`).

Because the resolved city is set before `nextCustomerCode(...)`, the existing case-insensitive customer-code logic is unaffected.

**New tests** (`OwnerRestControllerV1Tests.java`):
- `createOwnerTitleCasesCityWhenCityIsNew` — posts `"gOtHaM cITY"` (no existing owner there) and asserts the response `city` is `"Gotham City"`.
- `createOwnerReusesExistingCitySpelling` — posts `"MCFARLAND"` (seed data has an owner in `"McFarland"`) and asserts the response `city` is `"McFarland"`, proving the existing non-title-case spelling is reused rather than flattened to `"Mcfarland"`.
